![Threat Monitor screensaver](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kuydigital/threat_monitor/main/docs/screens.png)

A calm, at-a-glance read of world news while your computer is idle: one Global Threat Index plus war, disaster, cyber and outbreak scores, each with its latest headline. **New in 1.1: it now runs on Mac as well as Windows.** Created and maintained by Oliver Kuy.

[![Download for Windows](https://img.shields.io/badge/Download-Windows%20screensaver-0078D4?style=for-the-badge)](https://github.com/kuydigital/threat_monitor/releases/download/v1.1.0/ThreatMonitor-Windows.zip) &nbsp; [![Download for macOS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Download-macOS%20screensaver-1D1D1F?style=for-the-badge)](https://github.com/kuydigital/threat_monitor/releases/download/v1.1.0/ThreatMonitor-macOS.zip)

### Windows 10 and 11
Unzip the download and double-click **install.bat**. Screen Saver Settings opens with Threat Monitor selected; pick a wait time and click OK. If Windows shows "Windows protected your PC", click *More info*, then *Run anyway*.

### macOS 12 Monterey or later
Works on Apple silicon and Intel Macs. Open the download and double-click **Threat Monitor.saver**, then click *Install*. If macOS says it can't verify the screensaver, open *System Settings → Privacy & Security*, scroll down and click **Open Anyway**; you only do this once. Then choose Threat Monitor in *System Settings → Screen Saver*.

Prefer Terminal? This installs it with no security prompts:
`curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kuydigital/threat_monitor/main/mac/install.sh | bash`

### What's new
The Mac screensaver is a native app with the same news sources, scoring and screens as the Windows and Raspberry Pi versions, and automated tests confirm it gives identical scores and headlines. It shows on every display, drifts slowly to protect the screen, refreshes every 15 minutes and opens instantly with the last values. The war score no longer counts crime stories about "home invasions", and the Python version gains an **F** key to switch between a window and full screen.

<sub>Sources: BBC, Al Jazeera, NPR, Google News, GDACS, USGS, CISA and WHO. Threat Monitor measures how much is being reported, not real-world danger.</sub>
